5400: neuter of a derivative of φοβέω; a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent:--fearful sight.
5401: from a primary (to be put in fear); alarm or fright:--be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror.
5402: feminine of (bright; probably akin to the base of φῶς); Phœbe, a Christian woman:--Phebe.
5403: from φοῖνιξ; palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine:--Phenice, Phenicia.
5405: probably the same as φοῖνιξ; Phœnix, a place in Crete:--Phenice.
5406: from φόνος; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which ἀνθρωποκτόνος does not necessarily imply; while σικάριος is a special term for a public bandit):--murderer.
5407: from φονεύς; to be a murderer (of):--kill, do murder, slay.
5408: from an obsolete primary (to slay); murder:--murder, + be slain with, slaughter.
5409: from φόρος; to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment:--bear, wear.
5410: of Latin origin; a forum or market-place; only in comparative with Ἄππιος; a station on the Appian road:--forum.
5411: from φέρω; a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas τέλος is usually a general toll on goods or travel):--tribute.
5412: from φόρτος; to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety):--lade, by heavy laden.
5413: diminutive of φόρτος; an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service:--burden.
5414: from φέρω; something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship:--lading.
5415: of Latin origin; "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian:--Fortunatus.
5416: neuter of a derivative from the base of φραγελλόω; a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment:--scourge.
5417: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment:--scourge.
5418: from φράσσω; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively):--hedge (+ round about), partition.
5419: probably akin to φράσσω through the idea of defining; to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound:-- declare.
5420: apparently a strengthening form of the base of φρήν; to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence):--stop.
5421: of uncertain derivation; a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison):--well, pit.
5422: from φρεναπάτης; to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude:--deceive.
5423: from φρήν and ἀπάτη; a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer:--deceiver.
5424: probably from an obsolete (to rein in or curb; compare φράσσω); the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties):--understanding.
5425: apparently a primary verb; to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear):--tremble.
5426: from φρήν; to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience):--set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think.
5427: from φρονέω; (mental) inclination or purpose:--(be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed).
5428: from φρονέω; mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight:--prudence, wisdom.
5429: from φρήν; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while σοφός denotes practical skill or acumen; and συνετός indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative):--wise(-r).
5431: from a derivative of φρήν; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious:--be careful.
5432: from a compound of πρό and ὁράω; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect:--keep (with a garrison). Compare τηρέω.
5433: akin to βρύω, βρύχω; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult:--rage.
5434: neuter of a presumed derivative of (to roast or parch; akin to the base of φλόξ); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig:--stick.
5435: probably of foreign origin; Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor:--Phrygia.
5436: probably from φεύγω; fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian:--Phygellus.
5437: from φεύγω; a fleeing, i.e. escape:--flight.
5438: from φυλάσσω; a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively:--cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch.
5440: neuter of a derivative of φυλάσσω; a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts:-- phylactery.
5441: from φυλάσσω; a watcher or sentry:--keeper.
5442: probably from φυλή through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid:--beward, keep (self), observe, save. Compare τηρέω.
5443: from φύω (compare φύλλον); an offshoot, i.e. race or clan:--kindred, tribe.
5444: from the same as φυλή; a sprout, i.e. leaf:--leaf.
5445: from a prolonged form of (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to φύω through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough:--lump.
5446: from φύσις; "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive:--natural. Compare ψυχικός.
5447: adverb from φυσικός; "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively:--naturally.
5448: from φύσις in the primary sense of blowing; to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty):--puff up.
5449: from φύω; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage:--(man-)kind, nature(-al).
5451: from φυτεύω; trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable:--plant.
5452: from a derivative of φύω; to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine:--plant.
5453: a primary verb; probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively:--spring (up).
5454: of uncertain derivative; a burrow or lurking-place:--hole.
5455: from φωνή; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation:--call (for), crow, cry.
5456: probably akin to φαίνω through the idea of disclosure; a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language:--noise, sound, voice.
5457: from an obsolete (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare φαίνω, φημί); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative):--fire, light.
5458: from φῶς; an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy:--light.
5459: from φῶς and φέρω; light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively):--day star.
5460: from φῶς; lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively):--bright, full of light.
5461: from φῶς; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively):--enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.
5463: a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well:--farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.
5465: from the base of χάσμα; to lower (as into a void):--let down, strike.
5466: probably of Hebrew or (כַּשְׂדִּי); a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates:--Chaldæan.
5467: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious:--fierce, perilous.
5468: from a compound of χαλινός and the reduplicated form of ἄγω; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively):--bridle.
5469: from χαλάω; a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit):--bit, bridle.
5471: from χαλκός; a copper-worker or brazier:--coppersmith.
5472: from χαλκός and perhaps εἶδος; copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony":--chalcedony.
5473: diminutive from χαλκός; a copper dish:--brazen vessel.
5474: neuter of a compound of χαλκός and λίβανος (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre:--fine brass.
5475: perhaps from χαλάω through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it):--brass, money.
5476: adverb perhaps from the base of χάσμα through the idea of a fissure in the soil; earthward, i.e. prostrate:--on (to) the ground.
5477: of Hebrew origin (כְּנַעַן); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine:--Chanaan.
5478: from Χαναάν; a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine:--of Canaan.
5479: from χαίρω; cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight:--gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous).
5480: from the same as χάραξ; a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue):--graven, mark.
5481: from the same as χάραξ; a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation):--express image.
5482: from (to sharpen to a point; akin to γράφω through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege):--trench.
5483: middle voice from χάρις; to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue:--deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant.
5484: accusative case of χάρις as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of:--be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully.
5485: from χαίρω; graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude):--acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy).
5486: from χαρίζομαι; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty:--(free) gift.
5487: from χάρις; to grace, i.e. indue with special honor:--make accepted, be highly favoured.
5488: of Hebrew origin (חָרָן); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia:--Charran.
5489: from the same as χάραξ; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over):--paper.
5490: from a form of an obsolete primary (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval):--gulf.
5491: from a form of the same as χάσμα; a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water):--lip, shore.
5492: from the same as χειμών; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale:--be tossed with tempest.
5493: from the base of χειμών and ῥέω; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent:--brook.
5494: from a derivative of (to pour; akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter:--tempest, foul weather, winter.
5495: perhaps from the base of χειμών in the sense of its congener the base of χάσμα (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument):--hand.
5496: from χειραγωγός; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person):--lead by the hand.
5497: from χείρ and a reduplicated form of ἄγω; a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person):--some to lead by the hand.
5498: neuter of a compound of χείρ and γράφω; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)):--handwriting.
5499: from χείρ and a derivative of ποιέω; manufactured, i.e. of human construction:--made by (make with) hands.
